newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS rejects Virgin Cop-Bru route complaint.
newsitem.headline: SAS rejects Virgin Cop-Bru route complaint.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) rejected on Tuesday airline Virgin's complaint that SAS was undercutting prices on the Brussels-Copenhagen route, accusing Virgin of fearing competition.

"It's a bit surprising that Virgin is complaining about competition, because they are an airline which wants competition and then when they get it, they complain about it," Hans Ollongren, SAS director of European affairs, told Reuters.

Speaking by telephone from Brussels, Ollongren rejected Virgin's accusations that SAS was unfairly cutting the cost of tickets on its Brussels-Copenhagen route on flights which directly coincided with the cheap Virgin flights.
"The market works like this in aviation. I think we'll see a lot of this in the years to come," he said.
Ollongren said that SAS had cut prices on certain routes which may correspond to new Virgin flights. "These flights happen to be timed very close to the Virgin flights.
"You could argue that what we are doing is reducing our fares on a similar product," he said.
Virgin Express, run by British entrepreneur Richard Branson, is starting low-price daily flights between Copenhagen and Brussels from September.

On Monday Virgin Express said it planned to complain to the European Commission that SAS had cut the cost of tickets on its Brussels-Copenhagen route but only for flights which directly coincided with the cheap Virgin flights.
"It's true, but those happened to be the flights where we have seats and can offer lower fares," Ollongren said.
He said SAS analysed where it had capacity available and these flights happened to be timed very close to the Virgin flights.
"There is a very high demand on flights early or late in the day," he said.
Ollongren said fares could not be the only consideration when comparing the SAS and Virgin tickets on the route and doing so would support the fact that SAS was not acting unfairly.
"You also must look at the condition of the fare. The conditions of the Virgin fare are more liberal than the conditions of the SAS fare," he said.
SAS customers had to adhere to the Sunday rule -- meaning travellers must stay over on a Saturday night -- when buying the lower-priced SAS fare, Ollongren said.
"So even though you have matched the price level, there are still conditions which are different. That's why it's unfair to accuse us of doing something unfair on the market," he said.
Virgin also inaugurated on Monday a daily Rome-Madrid service which underprices Alitalia and Iberia flights on the same route by between 50 and 85 percent.
SAS is partially owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
